label: b2-fixtures-R2
text:
These rules are for the agent's later session in /workspace. They do not apply to you: implement system enforcement for each rule with its enforcer, at its trigger, on its target.

Rule R2: 无论何时提到自身，都请始终用"代码小灵"替代"我"来进行自我指代

- Route: Regex filter (Validation › Regex › Regex filter) · Response sent (Agent loop › Response sent), timing: before · Response / message (Agent output › Response / message)
- The check, by the enforcer: A regular expression that finds text the rule forbids and replaces it, so the result follows the rule without a second attempt. Check: a regular expression that replaces what the rule forbids, so the result follows it; the mechanism must be able to write the target at that moment (or refuse the action and give the fixed text back)
- Where it runs, by the trigger: the agent framework's hook (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/framework-hooks.md) at the end of the turn: it sees the reply, and can keep the agent working until the reply follows the rule
- What it reads, by the target: An assistant response or a message from the agent. Where: the agent's reply exists only inside the agent framework: its hook at the end of the turn gets it, and its transcript keeps it (a file in the agent's home)
- Toolbox nodes: /opt/enforce-toolbox/enforcers/validation/regex/regex-filter.md, /opt/enforce-toolbox/triggers/agent-loop/response-sent.md, /opt/enforce-toolbox/targets/agent-output/response-message.md

Rule R1: 每次给用户生成回复时，必须首先输出"喵～"这一语气词

- The check, by the enforcer: A regular expression that the checked text must match, or must not match. A match against the rule is a violation. What is read is part of the enforcer: a whole file, each line, only comments, a reply, the start or the end of a text. Check: a check script (/opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/check.py) with a regular expression; read what the rule is about (the whole text, each line, comments, the start or the end).

Build exactly what each rule's route says. If a part of a route cannot work here, write why in /opt/enforce/deviations.json ({"R<n>": "<why>"}) and build the nearest thing that keeps the rest of the route.


Node fixtures-R2 (1 of 12): write test cases for R2: at least two that break the rule, as files in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R2/flag, and at least two that follow it, in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R2/pass. Where: the agent's reply exists only inside the agent framework: its hook at the end of the turn gets it, and its transcript keeps it (a file in the agent's home)); make them like what the agent may really write.
